LOCAL

INTERACTIVE PREVIEW

Should I build this?

A small tool can be worth building if it solves something you repeat every day. Start with one useful moment and make it easy to try.

You could add a dashboard, a subscription, and a dozen integrations. But the first version only needs to help someone catch a useful sentence without losing the rest of the answer.

Keep the original text in place. Let people switch the lens off, choose what matters, and decide for themselves whether it helps.

Move over a paragraph. This preview works.
01 / A lens, right on the page.Original wording. Always.

A SMALLER KIND OF SOFTWARE

Fit into the way you read.

One job, a few controls, and an easy way out.

01

Turn it on.

Open Skim on an article or a long AI reply. A small dock appears at the top of the page.

02

Let your pointer linger.

The lens emphasizes an original sentence. Choose the answer, next steps, the catch, or key details.

03

Make it a habit.

Enable “Remember on this site” once. Skim returns there. Pause it globally or forget a site whenever you want.

YOUR BROWSER. YOUR WORDS.

The page stays
the page.

No moving paragraphs. No rewritten claims. No camera in the extension. Local sentence scoring runs in your browser, and the full context stays available.

Read the privacy details ↗
01

Only the sites you choose

One-off use needs a click. Automatic use asks for permission on that site.

02

A quieter reader, too

Open a page or a selected passage in a dedicated reader. Page text stays in the extension.

03

Easy to inspect. Easy to leave.

Download the GPL source, inspect the code, or remove the extension and its local settings.

THE EXPERIMENT THAT STARTED IT

What if it followed your eyes?

The webcam lab explores that idea with consent, calibration, and a quality check. It is experimental and separate from the extension. It does not measure comprehension.
